19307-the-lion-of-petra.title: The Lion Of Petra
19307-the-lion-of-petra.creator: Unknown
19307-the-lion-of-petra.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. So, since it can have no end and no beginning, you might define this as an episode--a mere interval between pipes, as it were, in the amusing career of Ali Higg ben Jhebel ben Hashim, self-styled Lion of Petra, Lord of the Wells, Chief of the Chiefs of the Desert, and Beloved of the Prophet of Al-Islam; not forgetting, though, that his career was even supposed to amuse his victims or competitors. The fun is his, the fury other people's.

34550-franz-joseph-haydn-the-story-of-th.title: Franz Joseph Haydn The Story Of The Choir Boy Who Became A G
34550-franz-joseph-haydn-the-story-of-th.creator: Unknown
34550-franz-joseph-haydn-the-story-of-th.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. It will be easy for you to remember the year in which Joseph Haydn was born, because you have already learned in school that our President, George Washington, whose picture should be inserted here, was born in the same year--1732.

arxiv-2102-13498.title: Constraining the Thickness of the Galactic Halo through Cosmic-Ray Anisotropy Using the Spatial-Dependent-Propagation Model
arxiv-2102-13498.creator: Bing-Qiang Qiao, Yu-Hua Yao *, Wei Liu, Qiang Yuan, Xiao-Jun Bi, Hong-Bo Hu, Yi-Qing Guo *
arxiv-2102-13498.description: Abstract The spatial-dependent-propagation (SDP) model with a nearby source works well to reproduce the coevolving features of both cosmic-ray (CR)-nuclei spectra and anisotropy. However, it is well known that the Sun is actually deviating from the galactic disk. This will lead to a dominating anisotropy in the direction perpendicular to the galactic disk, which is discrepant with current observations.

arxiv-2106-15993.title: Correlation energy and quantum correlations in a solvable model
arxiv-2106-15993.creator: Javier Faba, Vicente Martín, Luis Robledo
arxiv-2106-15993.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Javier Faba, Vicente Martín, Luis Robledo. Typically in many-body systems the correlation energy, which is defined as the difference between the exact ground state energy and the mean-field solution, has been a measure of the system’s total correlations. However, under the quantum information context, it is possible to define some quantities in terms of the system’s constituents that measure the classical and quantum correlations, such as the entanglement entropy, mutual information, quantum discord, one-body entropy, etc.

arxiv-2201-05062.title: Is magnetically dominated outflow required to explain GRBs?
arxiv-2201-05062.creator: Gregory Vereshchagin, Liang Li, Damien Bégué
arxiv-2201-05062.description: Abstract The composition of relativistic outflows producing gamma-ray bursts is a long standing open question. One of the main arguments in favor of magnetically dominated outflows is the absence of photospheric component in their broadband time resolved spectra, with such notable example as GRB 080916C.

arxiv-2304-08432.title: How Do Digital Advertising Auctions Impact Product Prices? Thanks: We acknowledge financial support through NSF Grant SES-1948692, the Omidyar Network, and the Sloan Foundation. An earlier version of this paper circulated under the title “Managed Campaigns and Data-Augmented Auctions for Digital Adv
arxiv-2304-08432.creator: Dirk Bergemann, Alessandro Bonatti, Nicholas Wu
arxiv-2304-08432.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Dirk Bergemann, Alessandro Bonatti, Nicholas Wu. We present a model of digital advertising with three key features: (i) advertisers can reach consumers on and off a platform, (ii) additional data enhances the value of advertiser-consumer matches, and (iii) bidding follows auction-like mechanisms. We contrast data-augmented auctions, which leverage the platform’s data advantage to improve match quality, and managed campaign mechanisms that automate match formation and price-setting.

arxiv-2406-06673.title: Instanton Density Operator in Lattice QCD from Higher Category Theory
arxiv-2406-06673.creator: Jing-Yuan Chen
arxiv-2406-06673.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jing-Yuan Chen. A natural definition for instanton density operator in lattice QCD has long been desired. We show this problem is, and has to be, solved by higher category theory. The problem is solved by refining at a conceptual level the Yang-Mills theory on lattice, in order to recover the homotopy information in the continuum, which would have been lost if we put the theory on lattice in the traditional way.

arxiv-2503-03366.title: Weak isotropy of central simple algebras with orthogonal involutions over totally positive field extensions
arxiv-2503-03366.creator: Priyabrata Mandal, Abhay Soman
arxiv-2503-03366.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Priyabrata Mandal, Abhay Soman. In this paper, we explore the behavior of orthogonal involutions in the context of totally positive field extensions. Let K / F K/F be a totally positive extension of formally real fields. By Becher’s result, if a quadratic form q q over F F becomes isotropic over K K , then q q is weakly isotropic over F F .

arxiv-2508-13005.title: Empirical Evidences for the Effects of Feature Diversity in Open Set Recognition and Continual Learning
arxiv-2508-13005.creator: Jiawen Xu, Odej Kao
arxiv-2508-13005.description: Abstract Open set recognition (OSR) and continual learning are two critical challenges in machine learning, focusing respectively on detecting novel classes at inference time and updating models to incorporate the new classes. While many recent approaches have addressed these problems—particularly OSR—by heuristically promoting feature diversity, few studies have directly examined the role that feature diversity plays in tackling them.

arxiv-2602-04398.title: Bi-directional Bias Attribution: Debiasing Large Language Models without Modifying Prompts
arxiv-2602-04398.creator: Yujie Lin, Kunquan Li, Yixuan Liao, Xiaoxin Chen, Jinsong Su
arxiv-2602-04398.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities across a wide range of natural language processing tasks. However, their outputs often exhibit social biases, raising fairness concerns. Existing debiasing methods, such as fine-tuning on additional datasets or prompt engineering, face scalability issues or compromise user experience in multi-turn interactions.

Influx of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) depends upon the expression and perivascular localization of the astroglial water channel aquaporin-4 (AQP4). Prompted by a...

pmc-11335246.title: Pharmacological induction of the hypoxia response pathway in Huh7 hepatoma cells limits proliferation but increases resilience under metabolic stress
pmc-11335246.creator: Clémence Jacquemin, Walid El Orch, Olivier Diaz, Alexandre Lalande, Anne Aublin-Gex, Florentine Jacolin, Johan Toesca, Mustapha Si-Tahar, Cyrille Mathieu, Vincent Lotteau, Laure Perrin-Cocon, Pierre-Olivier Vidalain
pmc-11335246.description: The hypoxia response pathway enables adaptation to oxygen deprivation. It is mediated by hypoxia-inducible factors (HIF), which promote metabolic reprogramming, erythropoiesis, angiogenesis and tissue remodeling. This led to the successful development of HIF-inducing drugs for treating anemia and some of these molecules are now in clinic.

pmc-11540994.title: A scoping review of rapid weight loss in judo athletes: prevalence, magnitude, effects on performance, risks, and recommendations
pmc-11540994.creator: Danilo F. C. dos Santos, Woo-Hwi Yang, Emerson Franchini
pmc-11540994.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). [Purpose] Combat sports, such as judo, are weight categorized. Weight control was established to promote fair disputes among individuals. However, combat sports athletes adopt rapid weight loss (RWL) to obtain an advantage over smaller and lighter opponents. This scoping review article presents the prevalence, magnitude, and methods of RWL and its effects on physical and competitive performance, health risks, and psychological effects.

pmc-11638695.title: Eco-Evolutionary Drivers of Vibrio parahaemolyticus Sequence Type 3 Expansion: Retrospective Machine Learning Approach
pmc-11638695.creator: Amy Marie Campbell, Chris Hauton, Ronny van Aerle, Jaime Martinez-Urtaza, Sean Hacking, Mehul Jani, Razvan Voicu
pmc-11638695.description: BackgroundEnvironmentally sensitive pathogens exhibit ecological and evolutionary responses to climate change that result in the emergence and global expansion of well-adapted variants. It is imperative to understand the mechanisms that facilitate pathogen emergence and expansion, as well as the drivers behind the mechanisms, to understand and prepare for future pandemic expansions.

pmc-11659126.title: Determination of weight loss methods and effects among wrestlers before an official championship
pmc-11659126.creator: Ramazan Seker, Ozkan Isik, Erdil Durukan, Meric Eraslan, Laurentiu-Gabriel Talaghir, Viorel Dorgan
pmc-11659126.description: IntroductionIt is known that combat athletes frequently lose weight before a competition. This study aimed to determine the weight loss methods before an official championship and the effects of these weight loss methods on the performance of wrestlers.MethodThe sample of the study consisted of 350 competitive wrestlers.

pmc-11862478.title: Catalyst effect of human body odours in social anxiety treatment – a pilot study.
pmc-11862478.creator: E Vigna, V Carli, C. Cecchetto, E. Dal Bò and C. Gentili from the Department of General Psychology, University of Padova, Padova, Italy. E. Eliasson, G. Hadlaczky and D. Wasserman from the National Centre for Suicide Research and Prevention of Mental Ill-Health, Karolinska
pmc-11862478.description: AbstractPOTION is an EU funded project (No. 824153) within the Horizon2020 initiative that aims at understanding the nature of chemosignals in humans and their sphere of influence on social interaction. The emotional state of one person can be transmitted to another through volatile molecules contained, for example, in the sweat.

pmc-12494201.title: Splenic torsion in polysplenia syndrome: a rare cause of acute abdomen in a paediatric patient
pmc-12494201.creator: Shaima Osman Mohamed Ali Alaraby, Sara Y Mukhtar, Mohamed Y Ibrahim, Eman Mohamed, Shima Abdalraheem Elnadeef Hussein, Mohamed Osman Mohamed Idres
pmc-12494201.description: Acute abdominal pain in children presents a significant diagnostic challenge due to its broad differential, including rare congenital anomalies. Torsion of an accessory spleen is a rare but important cause, particularly in the context of polysplenia syndrome. We report the case of a 6-year-old boy with polysplenia syndrome who presented with severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and diarrhea.

pmc-12577432.title: Fear of Movement: Validity and Reliability Study of the Turkish Version of the Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia for Headache in Patients with Migraine
pmc-12577432.creator: Dilara Onan, Halime Arıkan, Doğa Vurallı, Merve Ceren Akgör, Ayşenur Başel Pala, Ece Yanık, Ayşe İrem Can, Can Ulutaş, Pelin Yenilmez Yeşildaş, Burcu Karpuz Seren, İrem Yıldırım, Pınar Gelener, Esra Acıman Demirel, Esme Ekizoğlu, Aynur Özge
pmc-12577432.description: BackgroundWhile triggering by physical activity is a criterion for the diagnosis of migraine, evaluations regarding fear of movement related to physical activity are lacking in the literature. This study aimed to investigate the validity and reliability of the Turkish version of the Tampa Scale of Kinesiophobia, adapted to headache (TSK-H), in patients with episodic migraine (EM) and chronic migraine (CM).

pmc-12959616.title: Treatment of pulmonary fibrosis: From disease mechanisms to future novel therapies (Review)
pmc-12959616.creator: Sen Lu, Yunfei Liu, Xiaohua Li, Qipeng Yao
pmc-12959616.description: Pulmonary fibrosis (PF) is a progressive and fatal interstitial lung disease characterized by irreversible lung scarring and frequently associated with lung cancer. Currently, there remains a lack of effective therapies capable of significantly improving long-term outcomes or reversing the disease course. Although antifibrotic drugs are widely used and have enhanced the mechanistic understanding of PF, their efficacy is limited.

pmc-12967781.title: A STING-activating biomimetic mineralized nanovaccine triggers robust anti-tumor immunity
pmc-12967781.creator: Suxing Tuo, Yihan Wang, Meng Tian, Lixia Su, Jing Dong, Kefeng Lv, Wencan He, Qing Feng, Shan Chen, Daozhu Dong, Xiaoxu Li, Kejun Zhong, Yueming Zhang, Bo Kong, Lan He
pmc-12967781.description: Tumor nanovaccines have attracted great interest recently, due to a variety of advantages including high stability, efficient antigen packing and delivery, and the capacity to elicit sustained anti-tumor immune responses. Despite these advantages, existing nanovaccines are constrained by intricate manufacturing procedures and high production costs, prompting a need to develop simpler and more cost-effective solutions.

pmc-13057168.title: Linking lipid profile alterations to antibiotic tolerance and natural product synergy in drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis clinical isolates
pmc-13057168.creator: Anna Zabost, Rafał Sawicki, Grzegorz Jankowski, Marcin Ziomek, Wiesław Truszkiewicz, Arkadiusz Syta, Benita Hryć, Ewa Augustynowicz-Kopeć, Piotr Podlasz, Małgorzata Chmielewska-Krzesińska, Elwira Sieniawska
pmc-13057168.description: Despite global control efforts, tuberculosis remains the leading infectious cause of death, with rising incidence, pediatric cases, and drug-resistant strains posing major public health challenges. Mycobacteria, including Mycobacterium tuberculosis, possess a lipid-rich, dual-membrane cell envelope that contributes to their impermeability, drug resistance, and unique pathogenic mechanisms.

pmc-13217892.title: In vivo circRNA-engineered macrophages mediate localized MMP9 neutralization to rejuvenate aged bone
pmc-13217892.creator: Daoyu Zhu, Shifeng Ling, Haoyu Fang, Qianhao Yang, Yawei Du, Wenguo Cui, Yixuan Chen
pmc-13217892.description: Aging causes osteoporosis, delayed fracture repair, and osteoarthritis, but mechanisms and therapies remain unclear. Transcriptomics of serum and bone from older patients showed marked MMP9 upregulation, highlighting systemic MMP9 neutralization as a potential immunotherapy. Here, we developed an in vivo circRNA-based antibody-engineering strategy that specifically targets macrophages, converting them into biofactories for anti-MMP9 antibodies.

pmc-13282344.title: Prostate MRI quality improvement: a Roadmap from the ESUR Prostate MRI Working Group
pmc-13282344.creator: Adriano B. Dias, Jelle Barentsz, Clare Allen, Ronaldo Hueb Baroni, Hanna Falińska, Caterina Gaudiano, Rossano Girometti, Rajan T. Gupta, Fredrik Jäderling, Daniel Junker, Guido Matthias Kukuk, Ana Sofia L. Moreira, Vibeke Løgager, Philippe Puech, Andrei S. Purysko, Johannes Uhlig, Stephan Ursprung,
pmc-13282344.description: Prostate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has become a crucial tool in diagnosing and managing prostate cancer, mainly by helping to avoid unnecessary biopsies and enhancing the detection of clinically significant disease. However, its clinical usefulness is often limited by wide variation in how images are acquired, interpreted, and reported worldwide. This inconsistency affects diagnostic accuracy and patient outcomes.

pmc-13618282.title: Ionic Liquid Electrolytes for Extreme Temperature Conditions: Challenges and Perspective
pmc-13618282.creator: En Xie, Chengdong Liu, Xinghao Wang, Jian Wang, Zhen Chen, Huihua Li, Wenlong Cai, Hao Li, Yang Peng, Fanglin Wu, Stefano Passerini, Haolin Tang
pmc-13618282.description: The increasing applications of electrochemical energy‐storage systems in transportation, aerospace, and grid applications impose stringent requirements on electrolytes capable of operating safely and efficiently across extreme temperatures. Conventional carbonate‐ or ether‐ based electrolytes suffer from performance degradation and severe safety hazards in extreme thermal environments.

pmc-13653298.title: Oral Contraceptive Use Is Associated With Increased Tenderness to Palpation in the Masticatory System in Female Adolescents—Results of the Epidemiological LIFE Child Study
pmc-13653298.creator: Henriette I U Stasche, Gina M Georgi, Antje Körner, Wieland Kiess, Ronald Biemann, Jens C Türp, Christian Hirsch
pmc-13653298.description: BackgroundThe utilisation of oral contraceptives (OCs) has been demonstrated to be associated with the self‐reported occurrence of headaches in female adolescents. The objective of the present study was to determine whether the ingestion of OC was also associated with increased tenderness to calibrated palpation of the masticatory system.
